Subject: Sawtooth latency after privnet upgrade — production impact

Hi Ava,

We started seeing a sawtooth pattern in inference latency across our private cluster immediately after the PrivNet agent upgrade that landed at ~03:40 PDT this morning. Traffic to two customer-facing services is getting periodic 500/timeout spikes every 4–8 minutes for ~30–60s at a time.

Symptoms observed:
- Periodic spikes in P99 from ~120ms to ~1.2s with a sawtooth ramp down over 40–60s.
- Control plane reconnects reported in our application logs (agent reconnects + KV cache rebuild on reconnect).
- No obvious CPU/GPU saturation on nodes.

We attached a short metrics snapshot and a tarball of agent logs. Can you confirm whether this maps to any known post-upgrade regression on Redwood's side? This is impacting our throughput SLAs. We need an ETA on mitigation and whether a rollback is possible.

Attaching: controlplane-metrics-snapshot-20260815.png, privnet-diagnostics-20260815.tar.gz

Thanks,
Jill

Subject: INTERNAL: quick mitigation options for MedCore sawtooth pattern

Ava / team — runbook notes from initial triage:

Observations:
- Sawtooth pattern appears coincident with agent v2.14.0 deployment; reconnection/backoff code paths were modified to enable faster leader election and more aggressive prefix invalidation.
- On reconnection, the agent aggressively rebuilds KV cache which can lead to short bursts of higher token-latency while caches warm.
- Confirmed repeatable in our staging recreation with a scaled load generator.

Immediate mitigations (risk/benefit):
- Option A (fast): Roll back agent to v2.13.6 for MedCore cluster. Low risk, immediate (expected <20m to roll back per node), observed to eliminate sawtooth in staging.
- Option B (conservative): Disable fast-prefix invalidation flag remotely (feature flag) + throttle reconnect backoff. Medium risk; requires non-disruptive flag flip and monitoring.
- Option C (avoid for now): Full orchestration fix — will take longer (days).

Preferred path: Option A now, Option B as a staged fallback if A has side effects. We'll prepare rollback playbook and health checks.

Aditya — I can run the rollback commands and coordinate with Diego on stages. Dylan — can you prepare canary test and verification queries?

— Aditya
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Park <jill.park@medcore.com>

Date: 2026-08-15T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sawtooth latency after privnet upgrade — production impact

Jill — quick update from the bridge: we executed a per-cluster rollback to agent v2.13.6 at 10:20 PDT and observed the sawtooth spikes drop to background noise within two full cycles. The rollback ran node-by-node (no full cluster restart).

What we changed:
- Rolled agent image back to v2.13.6 (no config drift).
- Verified that reconnect/backoff stayed at previous cadence (no aggressive KV invalidation).
- Warmed KV caches via canary traffic to avoid cold rebuild spikes.

Attachments: privnet-diagnostics-20260815.tar.gz (logs pre/post), controlplane-metrics-snapshot-20260815.png

Status: Latency has returned to expected baselines. We'll continue monitoring for 72 hours and follow up with a postmortem and action items.

Please confirm if you want us to schedule a change window to re-run the v2.14.0 upgrade with additional guards, or prefer we hold on upgrades for your fleet until the patch is out.

— Ava

Subject: Post-incident summary and action items — MedCore PrivNet sawtooth regression

Hi Jill / MedCore team — thank you again for the quick collaboration on the bridge earlier this week. Below is a short post-incident summary, timeline, root cause, and our action plan. PDF attached (postmortem-action-items-20260818.pdf).

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-08-15 03:40 PDT: Agent v2.14.0 staged and rolled to MedCore cluster.
- 2026-08-15 03:48 PDT: First sawtooth latency events observed.
- 2026-08-15 09:10 PDT: MedCore ops reported to Redwood (this thread).
- 2026-08-15 10:20 PDT: Per-cluster rollback to v2.13.6 initiated by Redwood.
- 2026-08-15 10:30 PDT: Sawtooth pattern subsided; baselines restored.

Root cause: A regression in v2.14.0 introduced an aggressive prefix invalidation + reconnection behavior that caused agents to frequently rebuild KV caches under production load. This led to short, periodic latency spikes (the observed sawtooth). Staging tests did not fully mirror MedCore's traffic mix which amplified the effect.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back to v2.13.6 for affected clusters.
- Warmed KV caches on rollout to avoid cold-rebuild spikes.
- Added temporary alerting to surface similar reconnection counts and cache-warm metrics.

Planned follow-ups / action items (owner / ETA):
- INF-4823: Root cause fix in agent reconciliation logic + additional regression tests for cache-warm behavior (Aditya) — ETA 2026-08-23.
- Feature-flag path to opt out of the aggressive invalidation remotely (Diego) — ETA 2026-08-20.
- Canary re-roll plan with staged traffic shaping and pre-warm caches (Dylan) — ETA 2026-08-21.
- Offer: We'll apply a one-week service credit for impacted quota windows; PMs to confirm details (Ava) — ETA 2026-08-19.

Attachments: postmortem-action-items-20260818.pdf, privnet-diagnostics-20260815.tar.gz

If you’d like, we can schedule a short 30-minute readout next week to walk through the postmortem and proposed canary plan.

Thanks again and apologies for the disruption — we know production latency is critical for MedCore.

Best,
